feedback.label: Shoulder turn
feedback.message: Restricted shoulder turn at the top — less than most tour swings (loses coil/power).

feedback.label: Head sway
feedback.message: More lateral head movement than typical tour swings — head drifts off the ball during the swing.

feedback.label: Head height
feedback.message: More vertical head movement than typical — head rises/drops more than most tour swings.

feedback.label: Lead-arm extension
feedback.message: (low-confidence measurement) Lead arm more bent at the top than typical tour swings (less width/structure).

summary: 3 indicator(s) fall outside the typical tour range — see notes below.
llm_explanation:
At impact (the instant the club meets the ball), your hip rotation was about typical for a tour swing. At address (the setup position, just before the swing starts), your upper body leaned about as much as a typical tour swing. At impact, your upper body also leaned about as much as a typical tour swing. Your posture (the spine and body angle held during the swing) held about as steadily from setup to impact as a typical tour swing.

At address, your lead knee (the knee closer to the target) was bent about as much as a typical tour swing. At impact, your lead knee was bent about as much as a typical tour swing. Your hips slid toward the target about as much as a typical tour swing.

At the top (the top of the backswing, where the club changes direction), your shoulders rotated less than most tour swings. During the backswing (the takeaway and turn back, away from the target), your head drifted further side-to-side than most tour swings. In the downswing (the move from the top of the backswing down to the ball), your head moved more up-and-down than most tour swings. This gives you a solid base, and there is plenty here to feel good about.
